clinicalPearls: A severe X-linked contiguous gene deletion syndrome in which a deletion at Xq28 removes both ABCD1 and the adjacent DXS1357E locus, which corresponds to the gene BCAP31 (encoding B-cell receptor-associated protein 31).

It is far more severe than isolated X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy because loss of BCAP31, an endoplasmic reticulum chaperone involved in protein export and mitochondrial-ER interaction, adds a distinct developmental and hepatic disease.
Affected male infants present in the neonatal period with profound hypotonia, failure to thrive, cholestatic liver disease and, in many, primary adrenal insufficiency.
The biochemical signature of the ABCD1 defect persists: plasma very-long-chain fatty acids are elevated, as in X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy.
Neuroimaging typically shows a hypomyelinating or dysmyelinating leukoencephalopathy rather than the classic inflammatory posterior demyelination of childhood cerebral adrenoleukodystrophy.
The overlapping BCAP31-related phenotype (deafness, dystonia and central hypomyelination) explains features such as sensorineural hearing impairment seen in some infants.

Diagnosis rests on detecting the contiguous deletion by chromosomal microarray or targeted deletion analysis at Xq28, alongside raised very-long-chain fatty acids and evidence of adrenal and hepatic dysfunction.
Because it is a deletion of the whole ABCD1 gene, the newborn-screening C26:0 lysophosphatidylcholine marker used for adrenoleukodystrophy can flag these infants, prompting extended genetic analysis.
reference.pathophysiology: Contiguous ABCD1 DXS1357E deletion syndrome results from an interstitial deletion at chromosome Xq28 that simultaneously removes ABCD1 and the immediately adjacent locus historically designated DXS1357E, now known to be BCAP31. ABCD1 encodes the peroxisomal membrane transporter (ALD protein) required for import of very-long-chain fatty acids into peroxisomes for beta-oxidation; its loss produces the biochemical hallmark of accumulated very-long-chain fatty acids and predisposes to adrenal insufficiency and central nervous system demyelination, exactly as in X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy. BCAP31 encodes a widely expressed endoplasmic reticulum membrane chaperone that participates in quality control and export of membrane proteins from the ER and in coupling between the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria; its loss independently causes a syndrome of severe hypomyelination, dystonia, deafness and hepatic dysfunction. Because the two genes lie head-to-head and are deleted together, affected males suffer the combined consequences of both defects, giving a neonatal-onset, multisystem, and typically fatal disorder that is far more severe than adrenoleukodystrophy caused by intragenic ABCD1 variants alone. The precise deletion extent, and whether neighbouring genes are also involved, influences the exact phenotype.
additionalDifferentials: Isolated X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy / adrenomyeloneuropathy due to intragenic ABCD1 variants
Zellweger spectrum and other peroxisome biogenesis disorders with neonatal hypotonia and hepatic disease
Neonatal cholestatic liver disease of other genetic or metabolic cause
Congenital adrenal hypoplasia (including NR0B1/DAX1-related) presenting with neonatal adrenal insufficiency
additionalInvestigations: Plasma very-long-chain fatty acid profile (elevated, reflecting the ABCD1 component)
Chromosomal microarray or targeted Xq28 deletion analysis defining the contiguous ABCD1/BCAP31 deletion
Adrenal function assessment including cortisol and adrenocorticotrophic hormone response
Liver function tests and evaluation for cholestasis, with liver imaging as indicated
Brain MRI to characterise the hypomyelinating leukoencephalopathy
Audiological assessment for sensorineural hearing loss
Newborn-screening C26:0 lysophosphatidylcholine result and confirmatory molecular testing
redFlags: Neonatal adrenal crisis with hypotension and electrolyte disturbance requiring urgent recognition
Progressive cholestatic liver failure in early infancy
Rapidly evolving encephalopathy with profound hypotonia and feeding failure
A positive adrenoleukodystrophy newborn screen in a boy with additional hepatic or developmental features suggesting a contiguous deletion
reference.prognosis: The syndrome carries a very poor prognosis, with most affected male infants dying in early infancy from the combined hepatic, adrenal and neurological disease. Care is largely supportive, including adrenal hormone replacement and management of cholestasis, together with genetic counselling for the family.
pitfalls: Mistaking the disorder for isolated X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy and thereby underestimating the neonatal severity and hepatic involvement.
Overlooking BCAP31 as the gene underlying the DXS1357E locus, and so missing the mechanistic basis of the additional features.
Failing to pursue deletion analysis when standard ABCD1 sequencing is uninformative but very-long-chain fatty acids are raised.
Not recognising and treating adrenal insufficiency promptly in a critically ill neonate.
Attributing neonatal cholestasis to a primary hepatic cause without considering this contiguous deletion syndrome.
